basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 4.' and it opens 'Vers. 4. Excepto quod sanguinem cum carne non comedetis. Et hic et in lege Moysi esus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 4. Excepto quod sanguinem cum carne non comedetis. Et hic et in lege Moysi esus sanguinis prohibetur. In Actibus quoque apostolorum prohibitae sunt gentes a fornicatione, et immolatis, et suffocato, et sanguine (Act. XV, 20): quia videlicet sedes animae in sanguine est, ideo sanguinis prohibetur comestio.
